Kanuma is the third day of the Sankranti festival in Andhra Pradesh and is traditionally dedicated to honoring cattle, which play a vital role in agrarian life. Farmers decorate, clean, feed, and worship their cattle as a gesture of gratitude for their contribution to ploughing, irrigation, and transport. This day reinforces the bond between rural communities and their livelihood practices.

Key Insights:

• Kanuma is part of the four-day Makara Sankranti celebrations (Bhogi, Sankranti, Kanuma, Mukkanuma).

• Cattle - especially bulls and cows - are central to Kanuma rituals because of their importance in agriculture.

• Farmers traditionally clean cattle sheds, paint horns, and offer special feed called pindi vantalu.

• Kanuma emphasizes agricultural prosperity, livestock care, and rural sustainability.

• In some regions, decorated cattle processions and traditional sports are conducted.

• Kanuma highlights the dependence of traditional farming on cattle for ploughing and draught power.

• The festival fosters community bonding through shared rituals and feasts.

• It aligns with agrarian calendars marking the completion of the harvest season.

• Mukkanuma (following Kanuma) is associated with animal fairs and community celebrations.

• The festival underscores the cultural value of livestock wealth, considered a sign of prosperity in rural Andhra Pradesh.

The Great Indian Bustard (GIB), one of the world's most critically endangered bird species, was successfully reintroduced into the wild in 2025 at Desert National Park, Rajasthan. This park is the bird's last major natural stronghold and has been the center of India's conservation breeding and release efforts.

Key Insights:

• The Great Indian Bustard is listed as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List.

• Desert National Park covers the Thar Desert region across Jaisalmer and Barmer districts.

• The park provides ideal habitat - arid grasslands and scrub ecosystems - crucial for the bustard's survival.

• Conservation efforts include captive breeding, habitat restoration, and reducing power-line collisions.

• Rajasthan hosts the majority of the remaining wild GIB population.

• Sariska National Park is known for tiger relocation efforts but not for bustard reintroduction.

• Kuno National Park is India's site for the Cheetah reintroduction programme, not the GIB.

• Panna Tiger Reserve is known for vulture conservation and tiger recovery efforts.

• The GIB reintroduction involved collaboration between the Union Ministry of Environment, WII, and Rajasthan Forest Department.

• This success is a major milestone in preventing the extinction of one of India's most iconic grassland species.

The Asian Athletics Championships 2025 were hosted in Gumi, South Korea, where over 60 Indian athletes took part across track, field, and relay events. India sent one of its largest contingents to this edition of the championship.

Key Insights:

• The Asian Athletics Championships is a premier continental event organized by the Asian Athletics Association (AAA).

• Gumi was selected as the 2025 host city, marking South Korea's continued involvement in major athletics events.

• India fielded 60+ athletes, reflecting the nation's growing depth in track and field.

• Indian participation included top performers in javelin, long jump, shot put, 400m, hurdles, and relays.

• The event serves as an important benchmark for Asian and global rankings.

• Performances here contribute to qualification pathways for Olympics and World Championships.

• South Korea has previously hosted athletics championships in cities like Busan and Incheon, but 2025 was Gumi's first time.

• India's strong performance aligns with its increasing investment in elite training, sports science, and international exposure.

• Championships like these help emerging Indian athletes gain crucial competitive experience.

• The event also strengthens India - South Korea sporting cooperation, especially in athletics development and coaching exchange.

The Amateur Athletics Federation of India (AAFI), the original governing body for athletics in India, was established in 1946 to administer track and field sports, set national standards, and select athletes for international competitions. In 2000, it was renamed the Athletics Federation of India (AFI).

Key Insights:

• AAFI was formed in 1946, two years before India's independence, to formalize athletics administration.

• It became responsible for national championships, athlete selection, coaching camps, and rules enforcement.

• In 2000, AAFI was restructured and renamed as the Athletics Federation of India (AFI).

• AFI is the national body recognized by World Athletics (formerly IAAF).

• It oversees India's participation in global events like the Olympics, Asian Games, and World Championships.

• AAFI helped develop India's earliest athletics institutions and standardized competitions.

• Under AFI, India has seen improved performances in events like javelin, long-distance running, and racewalking.

• Prominent athletes associated with AFI's programs include Milkha Singh, PT Usha, Anju Bobby George, and Neeraj Chopra.

• The federation manages national training centres and collaborates with SAI (Sports Authority of India).

• Its establishment marked the beginning of organized athletics governance in modern India.

The circadian rhythm, which controls the body's 24-hour sleep - wake cycle, is regulated by the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) located in the hypothalamus.

The SCN receives light signals from the eyes and synchronizes body functions such as sleep, hormone release, body temperature, and metabolism.

Key Insights:

• The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) is the master clock of the human body.

• SCN uses light information from the retina to adjust the daily rhythm.

• It regulates melatonin secretion from the pineal gland - higher at night, lower during daylight.

• Hypothalamus also controls hunger, thirst, temperature, and hormone balance.

• Circadian rhythm influences alertness, mood, digestion, and immune function.

• Jet lag and shift work disrupt SCN functioning, affecting sleep cycles.

• Cerebellum manages coordination and balance, not circadian rhythm.

• Medulla oblongata controls breathing, heartbeat, and reflexes, not biological clocks.

• Thalamus mainly acts as a sensory relay station, not the regulator of circadian timing.

• The circadian rhythm is also supported by peripheral clocks in organs, but they all follow the SCN in the hypothalamus.

Glacial till is deposited directly by moving or melting glacier ice, meaning it does not undergo sorting by water. As a result, till contains a chaotic mixture of clay, sand, pebbles, cobbles, and boulders - all jumbled together in an unsorted, unstratified form. This contrasts sharply with glaciofluvial (water-laid) sediments, which are layered and sorted because flowing meltwater separates particles by size.

Key Insights:

• Glacial till is unsorted and unstratified, a major identifying feature.

• It consists of angular to sub-angular particles, since ice does not round sediments like water does.

• Till includes a full size range - clay to boulders - deposited simultaneously.

• Water-laid glacial sediments (outwash) are well-sorted and layered, due to meltwater action.

• Outwash plains are formed by running meltwater, not by direct ice deposition.

• Till forms landforms such as moraines, drumlins, and till plains.

• Outwash sediments form eskers, kames, and outwash plains.

• Glacial processes produce angular sediments; water processes produce rounded sediments.

• Option (1) and (2) describe water-laid deposits, not till.

• Option (4) refers to glacial lake sediments, which are typically finely layered (varves), not till.

Agro-based industries are those that use agricultural raw materials as their primary input.

Both cotton textiles (which use raw cotton) and sugar (which uses sugarcane) are classic examples of agro-based industries in India. These industries are closely linked with farming cycles, rural employment, and crop availability.

Key Insights:

• Cotton textile industry is India's largest agro-based industry, dependent directly on cotton cultivation.

• Sugar industry relies on sugarcane, is seasonal, and is located near cane-growing regions to prevent sucrose loss.

• Agro-based industries support rural livelihoods by creating employment close to agricultural zones.

• India is one of the largest producers of cotton, making cotton textiles a major export sector.

• Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Gujarat are major sugar-producing states.

• Cement and petrochemicals use minerals and hydrocarbons, placing them in heavy and chemical industries.

• Jute textiles are agro-based, but steel is a mineral-based heavy industry, so the pair does not fit.

• Edible oil is agro-based, but aluminum is produced from bauxite, making the combination unsuitable.

• Agro-based industries help reduce wastage of farm produce by converting crops into value-added products.

• These industries play a key role in India's food processing and textile economy, deeply linked to agricultural output.

The Right to Property was originally a Fundamental Right under Article 31, but it was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978. It was then made a legal right under Article 300A, meaning the State cannot take away a person's property except by authority of law.

Key Insights:

• The 44th Amendment shifted the Right to Property from Part III (Fundamental Rights) to Part XII (Legal Rights).

• Article 300A now states: "No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law."

• The change was made to reduce excessive litigation and allow smoother land acquisition for public purposes.

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, violation of Article 300A cannot be challenged directly in the Supreme Court under Article 32.

• Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, and Right against Exploitation continue to remain core Fundamental Rights.

• Property rights are still protected, but remedies now lie under High Courts (Article 226), not the Supreme Court directly.

• The right continues to apply to both citizens and non-citizens.

• The amendment was introduced after the Emergency period to rebalance powers between the State and citizens.

• Property rights remain important in taxation, land acquisition, and compensation laws.

• India is one of the few democracies where property rights are legal rights, not constitutional Fundamental Rights.

Gandhara art is not limited to its well-known stone sculptures of the Buddha. Archaeological discoveries from sites linked with the Gandhara cultural sphere - such as Bimaran and Begram - show a rich variety of artistic materials including gold, ivory, stucco, and imported luxury goods.

Both statements accurately reflect significant findings connected to the broader Gandharan artistic world.

Key Insights:

• The Bimaran casket (gold reliquary) is one of the earliest known Buddhist reliquaries, decorated with figures placed in an arcaded frame.

• This reliquary, found near Jalalabad (ancient Gandharan region), reflects Hellenistic influence in Buddhist art.

• The Bimaran gold casket is associated with early depictions of the Buddha in human form.

• Begram (Kapisa) yielded a remarkable hoard of carved ivory plaques, showing exceptional craftsmanship and trade connections.

• The ivories at Begram demonstrate links between India, Rome, and Central Asia, indicating the cosmopolitan nature of Gandhara.

• Begram's discoveries include not only ivories but also glassware, bronzes, and Chinese lacquer, illustrating vibrant long-distance trade.

• Gandhara art often blends Greco-Roman artistic features with Buddhist themes, seen across materials like stucco, gold, and ivory.

• The use of ivory reveals the presence of luxury objects produced in workshops possibly connected to the Mathura or South Indian ivory traditions.

• Findings from both sites highlight Gandhara's role as a cultural crossroads, absorbing artistic influences from the Mediterranean to India.

• These discoveries broaden our understanding of Gandhara beyond stone sculpture, showcasing a diverse artistic repertoire.

The 17th edition of the India - Mongolia joint military exercise Nomadic Elephant in 2025 was held in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. This exercise is part of ongoing bilateral defence cooperation focused on improving counter-insurgency, counter-terrorism, and interoperability between the two armies in challenging conditions.

Key Insights:

• Nomadic Elephant is an annual/biannual military exercise between the Indian Army and the Mongolian Armed Forces.

• The 2025 edition being hosted in Ulaanbaatar reflects alternating venues between the two nations.

• The exercise strengthens joint tactical operations, including room intervention, hostage rescue, and high-altitude drills.

• It supports India's broader Act East Policy and strategic partnership with Mongolia.

• Mongolia is a key partner for India in defence, culture (Buddhist ties), and rare-earth cooperation.

• India and Mongolia share a Strategic Partnership established in 2015.

• Previous editions have been held in locations such as Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, and Uttarakhand/Leh in India.

• The exercise enhances operational synergy, situational awareness, and tactical mobility of both forces.

• It also strengthens cooperation in UN peacekeeping operations, where both nations actively participate.

• Holding the exercise in Mongolia highlights India's role in supporting stability and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific and Eurasian regions.

The Union Council of Ministers (CoM) is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, as stated under Article 75(3) of the Constitution. This means the CoM must retain the confidence of the Lok Sabha to remain in office.

The second statement is incorrect because at the State level, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to the Legislative Assembly, not the Legislative Council, even if the state has a bicameral legislature.

Key Insights:

• Article 75(3): Union CoM is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

• This ensures parliamentary accountability and enables Lok Sabha to remove the government through a no-confidence motion.

• Collective responsibility means all ministers stand and fall together as one unit.

• Article 164(2): State CoM is collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly, not the Legislative Council.

• Legislative Councils (where they exist) have limited powers and cannot determine the survival of the state government.

• Legislative Assemblies (lower houses) directly represent the people, so accountability lies there.

• Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor, but practically this depends on majority support in the Assembly.

• This system establishes responsible government, where the executive is answerable to the elected legislature.

• Collective responsibility includes cabinet solidarity, meaning ministers must publicly support all decisions.

Sun-synchronous orbits (SSO) are special near-polar orbits in which a satellite passes over the same region of the Earth at the same local solar time each day. This provides consistent lighting conditions, which is especially valuable for remote sensing, imaging, and Earth-observation satellites.

Thus, Statement 1 is correct.

Statement 2 is incorrect because geostationary communication satellites are not sun-synchronous. They stay fixed relative to the Earth's surface at 35,786 km above the equator, not in polar orbits. Also, they do not rely on SSO for continuous solar power, as they already receive near-constant sunlight except during short equinox eclipses.

Key Insights:

• Sun-synchronous orbit (SSO): A near-polar orbit (~98° inclination) where the satellite's orbital plane precesses to match the Sun's apparent motion.

• SSOs ensure uniform lighting, essential for Earth imaging, climate monitoring, and agricultural mapping.

• Satellites like Cartosat, RISAT, NISAR, and Landsat commonly use SSO.

• SSO altitude is usually 600 - 800 km.

• Geostationary Orbit (GEO): 35,786 km altitude, equatorial orbit, satellite appears fixed to a point.

• GEO is ideal for telecom, broadcasting, and weather monitoring - not based on SSO principles.

• GEO satellites have nearly continuous sunlight, except brief seasonal eclipses.

• SSO is a subtype of sun-synchronous near-polar LEO, not suitable for communication satellites.

• The orbital mechanics of SSO rely on Earth's oblateness (J2 effect) to maintain consistent solar geometry.

Statement 1 is correct because Article 356(1) empowers the President to impose President's Rule based on a report of the Governor or otherwise. The Governor's recommendation is part of the constitutional mechanism, though not mandatory.

Statement 2 is incorrect because the 41st Constitutional Amendment (1976) dealt with raising the retirement age of High Court judges from 60 to 62.

It did not change the Governor's term, which remains 5 years under Article 156.

Statement 3 is correct. The Sarkaria Commission recommended that Governors should not be removed before the completion of their five-year tenure except in rare and compelling circumstances, to ensure the neutrality and stability of the office.

Key Insights:

• Article 356(1): Allows President's Rule when the State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

• The Governor's report is a common trigger but not the sole requirement for invoking Article 356.

• The 42nd Amendment, not the 41st, made wide-ranging structural changes; the 41st dealt only with High Court judges.

• Under Article 156, the Governor holds office for 5 years but "during the pleasure of the President," enabling removal anytime.

• Sarkaria Commission aimed to reduce misuse of Governor's office for political purposes.

• It emphasized appointing eminent, non-partisan persons as Governors.

• The Commission recommended Governors should act as constitutional guardians, not political agents.

• Removal before term damages Centre - State relations, hence the Commission insisted on rare exceptions.

• The discretionary role of Governors includes recommending President's Rule, reserving bills for President, etc.

• President's Rule requires parliamentary approval, making the final authority Union Executive + Parliament, not the Governor.

She is best known for translating The Diary of Anne Frank into Indian languages, which makes Statement 2 correct, while Statements 1 and 3 are incorrect.

Key Insights:

• Her translation contributions help make global literature accessible to Indian readers.

• She is not associated with Assam, making Statement 1 factually incorrect.

• She did not receive the Padma Bhushan in 2025; this confirms Statement 3 is incorrect.

• Translating world classics requires linguistic precision and cultural sensitivity.

• The Diary of Anne Frank is one of the most widely translated works globally, including in India.

• Translators like Gita Upadhyay play a key role in promoting cross-cultural understanding.

• Translation of Holocaust literature helps Indian audiences engage with global historical narratives.

• Padma awards recognize contributions in fields such as literature, but she was not among the 2025 recipients.

This is why India is often described as a "quasi-federal" or federal system with unitary features.

• Statement 2 is incorrect because the Indian Constitution does not use the word "federal" anywhere. Instead, Article 1 describes India as a "Union of States," emphasizing unity and indestructibility of the Union.

Key Insights:

• Article 1 calls India a "Union of States," chosen deliberately to indicate that states cannot secede.

• The Centre has wider powers in the Union List, including defence, foreign affairs, and banking.

• During emergencies, state powers significantly shrink, strengthening the central authority.

• Parliament can reorganize state boundaries under Article 3, reinforcing central dominance.

• Financial relations favor the Centre through central taxes and centrally sponsored schemes.

• The Supreme Court has termed Indian federalism as "cooperative federalism" and sometimes "competitive federalism."

• Despite central dominance, states retain autonomy in key areas like police, agriculture, and public health.

• The Constitution allows asymmetrical federalism, giving special provisions to certain states (e.g., Article 371).

• India's federal structure blends both federal character and unitary spirit, ensuring national unity while accommodating diversity.

questions.question: Which payload monitors solar wind at L1? L1 पर सौर पवन की निगरानी कौन सा पेलोड करता है?
questions.solution:
The ASPEX (Aditya Solar Wind Particle Experiment) payload onboard Aditya-L1 is specifically designed to study and monitor solar wind particles at the L1 (Lagrange Point 1) position. It measures the composition, behavior, and dynamics of charged particles emitted by the Sun.

Key Insights:

• ASPEX studies solar wind flux, energy levels, and particle spectra, crucial for understanding space weather.

• It helps predict geomagnetic storms that can affect satellites, power grids, and communication systems on Earth.

The least distance of distinct vision refers to the minimum distance at which a normal human eye can clearly see an object without strain.

For a healthy adult, this distance is approximately 25 cm. At distances shorter than this, the eye muscles face difficulty in maintaining focus.

Key Insights:

• The value 25 cm is also called the near point of the human eye.

• This distance increases with age due to reduced flexibility of the eye lens (presbyopia).

• Children often have a shorter near point because their eye lenses are more elastic.

• Reading books very close to the eyes causes eye strain because it requires continuous accommodation.

• Accommodation is controlled by ciliary muscles, which adjust the curvature of the eye lens.

• People with hyperopia (long-sightedness) have a near point farther than 25 cm.

• People with myopia (short-sightedness) may have a near point closer than 25 cm.

• Optical instruments like magnifying glasses are designed considering the 25 cm near-point standard.

• The far point of a normal eye is considered infinity, meaning distant objects are seen without accommodation.

• The least distance of distinct vision is a standard reference used in optometry and vision testing.

3) has - Grammatically incomplete; needs an object (e.g., has been breached).

4) had been - Past perfect; does not match the present-result clause alerts instantly.

Corrected Sentence:

If the security protocol is breached, the system alerts administrators instantly.

questions.question: Select the correct option: Although the experiment had been meticulously designed, unforeseen variables ___ the reliability of its conclusions.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct option:

Although the experiment had been meticulously designed, unforeseen variables ___ the reliability of its conclusions.
questions.solution:
The sentence describes a contrast: although the experiment was carefully designed, something negative affected the conclusions.

The only word that expresses weakening or reducing reliability is undermined.

Why the other options are incorrect:

2) bolstered - Means strengthened; opposite of what the sentence implies.

3) ratified - Means formally approved; does not relate to weakening conclusions.

4) exacerbated - Means worsened, but it applies to problems, not reliability. Reliability cannot be "exacerbated."

Corrected Sentence:

Although the experiment had been meticulously designed, unforeseen variables undermined the reliability of its conclusions.

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph: 1) Itis a process that involves the systematic and objective investigation of a subject to discover new facts or to confirm existing ones. 2) Research is a foundational pillar of academic and scientific progress. 3) This can be either theoretical, aiming to expand knowledge, or applied, seeking to solve a practical problem. 4) The findings of this investigation are then documented and peer-reviewed to ensure validity and credibility.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:

1) Itis a process that involves the systematic and objective investigation of a subject to discover new facts or to confirm existing ones.

2) Research is a foundational pillar of academic and scientific progress.

3) This can be either theoretical, aiming to expand knowledge, or applied, seeking to solve a practical problem.

4) The findings of this investigation are then documented and peer-reviewed to ensure validity and credibility.
questions.solution:
The most logical order for forming a coherent paragraph is:

2) Introduces the main idea - what research is and why it matters.

1) Explains the process of research (definition and purpose).

3) Adds detail about the types of research (theoretical vs. applied).

4) Describes what happens after the investigation - documentation and peer review.

This creates a smooth, natural flow from general → definition → types → outcome.

Why the other options are incorrect:

2) Starts with the process before introducing research; disrupts flow.

3) Begins with results ("findings"), which makes no logical sense as a starting point.

4) Starts with types before even defining research - illogical order.

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph: 1) A key strategy is to diversify energy sources, transitioning from fossil fuels to renewable alternatives like solar, wind, and geothermal power. 2) To mitigate the worst effects of climate change, the global community must drastically reduce its reliance on carbon-intensive energy production. 3) This shift not only decreases greenhouse gas emissions but also improves air quality and creates new economic opportunities. 4) Additionally, policies that promote energy efficiency in buildings and transportation can further lower overall energy consumption.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:

1) A key strategy is to diversify energy sources, transitioning from fossil fuels to renewable alternatives like solar, wind, and geothermal power.

2) To mitigate the worst effects of climate change, the global community must drastically reduce its reliance on carbon-intensive energy production.

3) This shift not only decreases greenhouse gas emissions but also improves air quality and creates new economic opportunities.

4) Additionally, policies that promote energy efficiency in buildings and transportation can further lower overall energy consumption.
questions.solution:
Sentence 2 states the problem and objective (reduce reliance on carbon-intensive energy), so it must open the paragraph.

Sentence 1 follows by presenting a principal strategy (diversify energy sources to renewables).

Sentence 3 explains the benefits of that shift (lower emissions, better air quality, new opportunities).

Sentence 4 adds an additional complementary measure (policies for energy efficiency).

The sequence 2 → 1 → 3 → 4 therefore moves logically from problem → solution → outcomes → further measures.

Why the other options are incorrect:

2) 1-2-3-4 begins with a strategy before the problem is stated, breaking the natural context.

3) 4-1-2-3 starts with an ancillary measure (efficiency) and places the core problem too late.

4) 2-3-1-4 puts the benefits before the main strategy, so outcomes appear before the action that produces them.

Change the following from active to passive:

The university may confer honorary degrees upon exceptional scholars.

options.html: Honorary degrees must be being conferred upon exceptional scholars by the university.

questions.solution:
Active Voice:

The university may confer honorary degrees upon exceptional scholars.

To convert modal + verb into passive:

may + be + past participle

So,

confer → be conferred

Thus the correct passive form is:

Honorary degrees may be conferred upon exceptional scholars by the university.

Why the other options are incorrect:

1) might have been conferred - Incorrect tense; changes the meaning to past possibility.

3) may have conferred - Missing "been"; grammatically incorrect in passive form.

4) must be being conferred - Wrong modal and incorrect continuous passive structure.

Example (to understand structure):

Active: They may award him a medal.

Passive: A medal may be awarded to him.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: PROPITIOUS
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: PROPITIOUS

Propitious means showing good signs or being likely to bring success; favorable or advantageous.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: It remains unclear whether the board intends to implement the proposal (1)/ or if the statement was merely a strategic ploy (2)/ aimed at appeasing shareholders (3)/ in light of the recent legal setbacks. (4)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

It remains unclear whether the board intends to implement the proposal (1)/ or if the statement was merely a strategic ploy (2)/ aimed at appeasing shareholders (3)/ in light of the recent legal setbacks. (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in part 2: "or if the statement was merely a strategic ploy".

Rule:

When using "whether", the parallel construction should be "whether.. or", not "whether.. or if."

So the correct structure must be:

whether the board intends to implement the proposal OR the statement was merely a strategic ploy

Adding "if" breaks the parallelism and is grammatically incorrect.

Why other parts are correct:

1) Correct - Clear and grammatically sound.

3) Correct - Proper participial phrase "aimed at appeasing shareholders."

4) Correct - Contextual and grammatical; no error.

Corrected Sentence:

It remains unclear whether the board intends to implement the proposal or the statement was merely a strategic ploy aimed at appeasing shareholders in light of the recent legal setbacks.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The presumption, not that the policies themselves were ill-conceived but rather that their rhetorical framing - laden with abstractions alien to grassroots discourse - (1)/ have contributed more to civic apathy (2)/ than implementation failures per se, reflects a deeper institutional detachment (3)/ than previously acknowledged. (4)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The presumption, not that the policies themselves were ill-conceived but rather that their rhetorical framing - laden with abstractions alien to grassroots discourse - (1)/ have contributed more to civic apathy (2)/ than implementation failures per se, reflects a deeper institutional detachment (3)/ than previously acknowledged. (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in part 2, where the verb "have contributed" is incorrectly used.

Rule:

The subject of the clause is "The presumption", which is singular.

Therefore, the verb must also be singular → has contributed, not have contributed.

So the correct form is:

"..has contributed more to civic apathy.."

Why other parts are correct:

1) Grammatically complex but correct; the clause correctly offsets the contrast.

3) Correct - "reflects" agrees with the singular subject "presumption."

4) Correct - No grammatical issue.

Corrected Sentence:

The presumption .. has contributed more to civic apathy than implementation failures per se, reflects a deeper institutional detachment than previously acknowledged.

questions.question: Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word: The legal scholar revised the digest of civil statutes.

The legal scholar revised the digest of civil statutes.

questions.solution:
The highlighted word digest in the given sentence means a summary or compilation of information (noun).

A homonym must:

• have the same spelling

• have the same pronunciation

• carry a different meaning

Option (1) uses digest in a different sense → to digest food (verb form used as a noun in informal/incorrect phrasing, meaning "digestion"). This fits the requirement of a homonym because it represents a completely different meaning from "summary."

Why the other options are incorrect:

2) "digest" = a summarized publication - same meaning as the highlighted word.

3) "digest" = a compilation - same meaning again.

4) also "digest" = summary or compilation - again same meaning.

Example:

• I read a digest of legal cases. (summary)

• Your body needs time to digest food. (process of digestion)

questions.question: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence: He walked slowly lest he should fall.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

He walked slowly lest he should fall.

options.text: so that he may not fall
options.html: so that he may not fall

questions.solution:
The conjunction lest is always used to express fear, prevention, or negative purpose.

Grammar rule:

After lest, we use a bare infinitive (V1) - NOT "should fall" or "may fall".

So the grammatically correct construction is:

lest + subject + bare verb

→ lest he fall

Why the other options are incorrect:

1) in order to not fall - "In order to" expresses purpose, not fear; also incorrect structure with "not."

2) so that he may not fall - Changes meaning; "lest" already carries the sense of prevention.

4) for fear of falling - Meaning is similar but it rephrases the sentence instead of replacing the highlighted part correctly. The question requires keeping the original structure.

Corrected Sentence:

He walked slowly lest he fall.

questions.question: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence: He speaks English good .
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

He speaks English good.
questions.solution:
The word good is an adjective, but here it is describing how he speaks, which requires an adverb.

The correct adverb form of "good" is well.

So the correct replacement is "He speaks English well."

Why the other options are incorrect:

1) very good - Still uses an adjective; grammatically incorrect in this context.

2) nicely - Grammatically correct adverb, but it does not mean "with skill or proficiency."

3) fluently - Correct meaning in some contexts, but it changes the meaning. The question requires correct grammar, not a different idea.

Corrected Sentence:

He speaks English well.

questions.question: Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure: The instructions have been misunderstood by many candidates.
questions.questionHtml:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The instructions have been misunderstood by many candidates.

options.text: Many candidates have misunderstood the instructions.
options.html: Many candidates have misunderstood the instructions.

questions.solution:
Passive Voice:

The instructions have been misunderstood by many candidates.

To change to active voice, identify:

• Object in passive → Subject in active: many candidates

• Verb: have been misunderstood → have misunderstood

• Subject in passive → Object in active: the instructions

So the active form becomes:

Many candidates have misunderstood the instructions.

Why the other options are incorrect:

1) "misunderstood" (simple past) - changes the tense from present perfect to past.

3) Grammatically incorrect and nonsensical.

4) "misunderstand" (simple present) - changes the tense completely.

questions.question: Spot the correct spelling of a happy accident adjective.

questions.solution:
The adjective serendipitous means occurring by chance in a happy or beneficial way. This is the correct spelling.

Why the other options are incorrect:

2) Serendipidous - Incorrect; wrong placement of i.

Their meeting was completely serendipitous, yet it changed everything.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of idiom: Fiddle while Rome burns
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the correct meaning of idiom:

Fiddle while Rome burns

options.text: To waste time in trivialities during a crisis
options.html: To waste time in trivialities during a crisis

questions.solution:
The idiom "fiddle while Rome burns" refers to ignoring a serious problem and doing something trivial or self-indulgent instead. It originates from the legend that Emperor Nero played the fiddle while a massive fire destroyed Rome.

Why the other options are incorrect:

1) To play music at night - Literal meaning; not connected to the idiom.

3) To seek artistic approval - No relation to neglecting a crisis.

4) To incite rebellion - Opposite context; idiom is about apathy, not agitation.

Example:

The manager was fiddling while Rome burned, discussing logo colors while the company system was crashing.

questions.question: A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech. He said that he wished to speak with the manager.
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

He said that he wished to speak with the manager.

options.text: "I wish to speak with the manager," he said.
options.html: "I wish to speak with the manager," he said.

options.text: "I want to speak with the manager," he said.
options.html: "I want to speak with the manager," he said.

options.text: "I wished to speak with the manager," he said.
options.html: "I wished to speak with the manager," he said.

options.text: "May I speak with the manager?" he said.
options.html: "May I speak with the manager?" he said.

questions.solution:
In indirect speech, the verb "wished" often reports a polite request or desire.

When converting back to direct speech, we restore the original tense unless it was originally past due to context.

Here, wished → wish in the direct form.

Indirect: He said that he wished to speak with the manager.

Direct: "I wish to speak with the manager," he said.

Why the other options are incorrect:

2) "I want to speak.." - Changes the meaning; "wish" and "want" are not identical.

3) "I wished to speak.." - Incorrect because direct speech normally restores the present tense.

4) "May I speak..?" - Turns a statement into a question; changes meaning entirely.
